“我打得这么准，评价肯定很高吧” *五音不全* “？” “卧槽怎么一下节奏都跟不上，攻击全部刮痧，还好走位灵活，敌人一下都摸不到我” *五音不全* “？” “又要瞄准又要卡点，还要走位，太难了吧” *五音不全* “？” “怎么有刺，怎么有锯子，我怎么扣血了” *死亡：敌人投射物* “？” “冷静模式？不需要卡点就能打伤害？瞧不起谁呢” *死亡：敌人投射物* “？” “换个音乐，这个节奏快” *万籁之音* “这才是真正的技术。” “还有自定义音乐？我去，来一首《Operation Pine Soot》” *万籁之音* “你知道的，我一直是《ROBOBEAT》的粉丝，这完全是来自Kwalee Ltd的艺术品，制作精良，操作流畅，音乐带感，多种武器，支持导入自定义音乐。一场伟大的战斗，可以让优秀的玩家变得更加优秀。” 一些小疑惑： ·武器说明不太能看懂 ·枪声似乎有点延迟，以至于枪声难以对应节奏，导致后续节奏乱掉 ·乒乓球的手感有点——或者说没有手感，需要三次攻击才会发射子弹，不是很喜欢这把武器 ·进入奖励房和卡牌房时，音乐的音量会骤然降低，缺少平滑过渡

[h1] 手感爽快，系统稀烂。 [/h1] 【优点】战斗爽！可自定义音频！ 【缺点】堆数值，rogue解锁太慢，枪械平衡性存在问题。 [h2] 手感良好 [/h2] 游戏的射击手感相当不错，是目前最类似ultrakill的节奏射击。 射击的音效和视觉效果都有很好的打击感。配合游戏的节奏系统，这款游戏只玩打枪部分都很有意思。 角色移动丝滑，显然不如ultrakill手感这么爽，但既不飘，也不会显得角色笨重，可以给个良好。 游戏有格挡操作，但大部分伤害还是需要躲避处理（格挡这类招式大概率跟不上节拍）。诚然游戏做了一些有时间窗口的可格挡伤害，但它们和普通攻击混在一起，显然容易成为游戏的干扰项。 [h2] roguelite [/h2] [h3] 内容解锁慢 [/h3] 每把枪、每个新能力都需要使用局内获取的点数来解锁。这但完成一局游戏获取的点数远远不足，想要解锁新功能，必须玩上好几局。 尽管枪支解锁速度慢，但敌人的数值成长可快了！初始枪很快就会疲软无力，后续只能靠奖励房间抽取 [h3] 平衡性不行 [/h3] 几把枪的平衡性明显存在问题，如果缺乏快速清小怪的（接触、乒乓球等）能力，这游戏真的很难玩。 游戏的数值堆叠问题严重，在1~2章中可以用的攻击手段，在第三章马上就变得根本不够看。 卡牌build上下限差距极大，存在非常超模的卡，也有大量根本用不上的卡牌。所以要是运气不好，没有抽到好用的枪/卡牌，这局游戏根本就可以不用打了。 [h3] 地图设计中庸 [/h3] 如果你是从隔壁hellsinger来的，那么这个游戏的地图体验会比hellsinger好出不少：小怪颜色区分度高，地图中没有太多遮挡。 简单来说，不需要找怪。 但如果你是从ultrakill来的，那么这游戏的地图设计又有点不够看：大量不知道为啥存在的陷阱（一不小心就会踩上去）；刷怪要等好几秒，中断了我的输出心流；房间数量有限，玩得稍微久一些就会没意思。 [h3] 回血机会少 [/h3] ultrakill靠近距离杀死敌人回血，既鼓励玩家铤而走险，又让玩家自己掌握了战斗风格。但这个游戏偏偏把这个设定给取消了，而其他回血机会又非常少。导致我打得提心吊胆，很难战斗爽。

总体来说瑕不掩瑜，但我在其中获得的挫败感大于愉悦感，因此不推荐。以下是令我难受的点： 1、简略的教学。游戏教学仅仅揭示了基本操作，却没有提示玩家具体如何使用。比如，在翻找评论区前，我并不知道格挡还能够弹射炸药桶，而这一点仅仅体现在游戏中的一行提示里。又如，我玩了好几局以后才意识到不同武器可以通过蓄力-弹反来组合出不同的攻击特效。 2、较高的认知负荷。在这一款游戏中，玩家通常需要同时注意以下几件事：节拍、跑酷、招架、瞄准设计、技能、陷阱。值得注意的是，一般人类的大脑难以同时处理多个任务，我很难一边在高速移动中进行瞄准，一边规避地上的陷阱，一边通过招架和跑酷来规避攻击。游戏中并不清晰的弹反判定和攻击提示，以及FPS的视野盲区则雪上加霜。个人认为制作组应该想办法优化（至少是新手的）认知负荷。 3、挫败感。前文提到，游戏的认知负荷较高，这使得每局游戏都需要高度集中精力。可是，我往往一局游戏只能解锁一个新项目，且死亡后不能留下任何东西，这带来了很强的挫败感，让我玩了几局就不想再继续了。

Pretty solid overall, but doesn't do much to stand out from the crowd as far as roguelikes go. Visuals are muddy and cluttered. There's no audio feedback upon taking damage which makes it hard to tell when you get hit at all given the music-focused nature of the gameplay. The custom music system is very sophisticated, though; being able to import any song you want to serve as the game's BGM is a pretty nutty concept. A bit rough around the edges, but shows a lot of potential!

Finally finished the game after being stuck on the horribly long final boss fight. (only 3.3% of ALL players have beaten the game on Steam) There are some things I really like about this title and its a great concept as a whole. but...Holy moley there are some insanely annoying bugs and really stupid mechanics/design choices that make me never wanna play again and really hesitantly recommend it. Positives: -movement feels pretty good, slam jumping, wall jumps and dashes all feel pretty solid. near ultrakill levels but not quite as complex and with lower speed -some weapons are designed fairly well and feel/sound great to shoot on beat -adding your own music is fun (when it works..ill get to that) -the first 3 bosses are awesome to fight -loads of secrets and unlocks thats about it..honestly, past that its really hard to give the game any more compliments. here is some bugs as well as design choices that really hinder the experience. I'll list bugs first: - (bug) adding your own music will have it automatically try to guess/fill in the beat spots. out of the 15 songs I added, about 11 of them had serious issues at several points in the song that needed fixing - (bug) the custom volume slider for songs freaks out constantly and will not save your choice, often resulting in tracks that are super loud or too quiet. - (bug) parrying any attack that is not the (!) homing track shots works about half the time.. seriously. parrying on beat is supposed to result in "increased range of the parry" but this also doesnt work for any non homing shot. often making you whiff and take a ton of damage - (bug) when changing keybinds for equipment, the HUD will show the incorrect prompt no matter what you do - (bug) jumping will make the beat indicator by the aiming reticle stagger which counts for a shot's beat causing ruined beat streaks and damage - (bug) especially in later levels, some enemies will get stuck on terrain/stop attacking. sometimes just until you turn a corner then they are already mid animation attacking you Negatives: -some weapons are downright useless. Now I get its a roguelike and not every random loot can be overpowered, but its so bad that genuinely wish some would never show up. (shield and kunai in particular) -damage is incredibly high, especially on further levels and if you have a gun augment that can make you take more? expect to get 2 shot by nearly everything. Unless you have the best of the best upgrade cards. -like the weapons, certain utility items and upgrade cards are also completely useless -no use for blips/unlock currency whatsoever after youve unlocked everything you can. Genuinely, why even have the doors show up then? why give the currency on boss kill? The ability to buy a heal instead, an upgrade, or ANYTHING would be better than this. -the last boss is an absolute slog, I'm talking a 5+-7+ minute fight unless you have the best dps possible at that point, with no option to heal beforehand. Seriously why does this guy have so much health? You better play near perfect and know every one of his attacks otherwise you're toast. Took me 7+ attempts and I never wanna do it again. ---------------------------------------------- I know this was a long review, and it honestly really sucks I'm this bent out of shape about it, because I think there's a great game in here, but these issues have gotta get fixed, and I'll change my opinion if they do. Otherwise, maybe consider staying away.

Game is alright. But the cons just make the game not worthwhile. Literally half of the people that've played the game haven't made it halfway, and only 3% have beaten the final boss. Problems: - Music gimmick sucks. Just give me a song per level; forcing me to pick one song for basically the entire run is wack. - Most abilities and guns are bad. The starter stuff is literally the best and unlocking the other stuff just clogs your pool. - Enemies are so bland. Ground enemies are all blockfigures and flying enemies are all eyeballs. - Parry is jank. Won't work sometimes and works sometimes when it shouldn't. - Not really keyboard friendly with all the keybinds - Roguelike part is weirdly done, makes you restart every time you get to the next floor. For example, if its your first time beating floor 2, it makes you restart.

Still on the hunt for a rhythm shooter that does the job completely. BPM suffered from poor telegraphs and enemies that failed to follow any semblance of a beat pattern, but the gunplay felt more in touch with the beat. Robobeat is the inverse, with enemies that (mostly) follow the beat pattern, but where gunplay overall feels like you spend more time cheesing combat outside of a beat pattern's flow state. Is it so much to ask to combine both into one game? Robobeat is generally stronger than BPM for bosses and challenge. It falls short when only a few weapons are effective or even fun to use, and most unlocks are so bad that I suggest not even buying more than maybe Contact and calling it a day there so your pool isn't diluted. The base starting revolver really shouldn't feel like the strongest possible in the entire game, but it is. As soon as you learn to aimbot parry, you're actively gimping yourself if you drop it, but simultaneously gimping yourself by keeping it because your damage is going to be abyssmal. If you don't unlock any weapons, you can only drop get revolvers from random drops, so you're better off with both damage and capabilities. If you do buy unlocks, pick your poison: Keep the revolver and do minimal damage, or change it out and deal with a gun that shoots a beat after you pull the trigger. Fun choice, right? It still doesn't show its cracks until the last run. The initial three bosses are difficult to start, but decently fun once you learn their patterns. The final is a whole other story. Not only does it not perfectly follow its own supposed patterns (I've had the parry window be on the backbeat multiple times), even with a strong defensive build, you'll be wiped in around 5-6 hits, and a build that tanked out is rare. You'll mostly get trashed in 3. But you can just power through and win, right? Just a couple more hits, you've been at this perfectly for around 3 minutes, there's no way he has much more health, surely. Think again. You're about 1/3 through if your build is good. Any one of the negatives I could look past on their own, but piling a misbehaving bossfight that last nearly 10 minutes on the end of a run that already took you 30-40 minutes to do with no option to practice just tastes awful. Could have been a fun, even if slightly difficult, diversion if the final boss hadn't soured it beyond belief. Extra edits as I remember more annoyances: -Speaking of time, the time gate requirement per level is far too tight. I'm not bad at the game by any means, but even with fast room clears because of good utilities, I still tended to be 20 seconds over the timer. I don't know what kind of output the time limit was balanced for, but it certainly wasn't for general gameplay. Add on top of that that the rewards are basically never worth it anyway, and I just found myself ignoring the mechanic completely.

- Mom, I want Ultrakill!!! - We have Ultrakill at home, honey. I mean seriously, this is basicly just Ultrakill, but with less weapon swapping. And with ~meh soundtrack and guns. The main problem I have with this game is not having a unique music for each level. Levels themselves are bland and basicly the same, but having a repeated songs on top of that makes the whole run feel like you are stuck on the same level over and over again. Also, if you do not make your own mixtape (or find one premade) - you have to manually switch songs or be stuck with the same looping song. Another problem is lack of enemy variety. It's just dudes, flying eyes and sentries. Maybe there will be more after I will beat the "campaign", but so far it's not interesting to fight them. Same as beating the rooms: they are small-ish, with enemies slowly spawning in waves. This just slows the pace of the game down for no real reason. Lastly, the Ultrakill comparison. I do not like the "combo" games. They are rewarding if you know what you are doing, but I personally just do not want to learn the "push barrel into enemy while running on a wall to then do a 360 and then shoot him in a head with a charged parry strike to get 30 COOL POINTS!!!". Game is beatable with minimum combos and a single gun, but it's boring. If you are looking for a good rythm shooter - play BPM: Bullets Per Minute or Metal: Hellsinger. Robobeat is just not it.
The music is good, but the gameplay is to limited and the gun fights way to long for its own good.

设计理念不错，能加自定义歌曲好评。 然而关卡实际游玩累得要死，比起其他fps爽游，感觉体验更像数值填的更糟糕，道具更没用的dead cells + isaac。 1.敌怪攻击力相当高。一发弹幕25血，弹幕多，回血少，容错低，所以非常依赖反击。 2.武器之间的区别几乎不影响推进速度，等级上去了伤害自然高。 3.被动几乎都没什么用，剩三个反击回血的、交替射击加攻、20%处决，抽得到就打得轻松，抽不到就多摁反击。 以上三点导致流派其实不重要，每局就是看运气找武器和被动，跟着节奏按左右键，然后摁反击。 打到最后一关，最后boss过不去，感觉太累没动力打下去了。 前面难度其实也不算高，但打到最后一关的成就完成率只有9.1%，要入的话先考虑考虑，demo玩个两小时，大概也明白这游戏的游玩体验大概啥样了。 还有美术上每关都是同一个色调，完全兴奋不起来。 很欠打磨

When BPM released it quickly became one of my favourite games, so I had high hopes for this since it seemed heavily inspired by BPM. What I played seemed to be a mix of BPM and Ultrakill (though I never played Ultrakill). The focus is heavily on combos, skills and parrying, less on roguelike. I missed feeling like I became more powerful through thinking out my build, since you mostly decide on 2-3 weapons + 2-3 skills and a few upgrades during your runs. Outside out of that all you had was your skill in the moment. When I was hitting my parries and skill checks it felt satisfying, but not enough to overcome the frustration of all the inconsistent parry windows, homing shots and teleporting enemies. There's a very high skill ceiling, but also a high skill floor, though you can lower beat difficulty if you feel like it. I dropped the game a few times, and forced myself to try again until beating the last boss since it seemed there was a fun game under there from time to time. I feel like it suffered a bit from being a one dev game, for example its clearly a KB+M, but the UI feels very inconsistent or controller like. Some other confusing stuff like the floors, or the upgrade system feeling sometimes detrimental to my build choices. The music importer is neat, easy to just import a looping track from an OST from your favourite game All in all for a one man developed game it's still impressive, a great game for hardcore fps mobility lovers, but less for roguelike elements

I think for some people this game can be awesome, but its a niche genre(rhythm game) mixed with a niche genre(roguelike) mixed with a first person shooter(popular but probably not the most overlap with all the other genres) and then boxed in entirely by another niche genre(soulslike). The soulslike genre is the one that seems to fit all the off-putting parts of the game such as clunky controls, punishing parry-based combat with no checkpoints, minimal healing, and no difficulty setting. I do happen to sometimes enjoy all of those things, but rarely if ever would i be in the mood for all of them at the same time, so this game ends up being kind of hard to try and play despite having some pretty cool stuff about it. If you like all those things consistently, then consider this a recommended. I chose not recommended though because its so ultra specific gameplay that isn't entirely clear without researching the game, and its done in such a way that even playing all those sorts of games at times i still often would rather play something less likely to just randomly kill you or something that leans into the music part of the music game more. When you are in the right mood for it or this combo just works for you in general, it can be great fun to jump and dash around like a lunatic while trying to stay on beat. Most of the time though, that fun streak often gets interrupted a bit when ending like the fourth or fifth run in a row with zero lasting progress due to something like moving 1 foot in the wrong direction and touching a trap(or any enemy in any non-dead state), or because you looked at the wrong one of the, usually spawned in pairs, enemies that make a noise then shoot an undodgeable attack at you that can still auto hit you from such a distant spot they're barely even visible. When i say no checkpoints- it resets you to a hub when you die, though i guess since there are kind of different unlocked levels to enter in the hub so maybe people could consider those as checkpoints. However they do not really function as checkpoints to start from a point later in the game. its still a roguelike structure so you have to always start at the first level, it just cuts you off at a point and sends you back initially to unlock a second door which is still the first level but a little harder and with a further cutoff point. Each new level kinda just does that, you get stopped at the end and reset so you can play all the previous levels made harder and with a new chunk added at the end. A lot of the difficulty can change based on song speed, and there's probably like a sweet spot for each person depending on how fast they like to play, so that is a cool bit of variation and might be the closest thing there is to tweaking the difficulty. However, it can't properly do too high or too low BPM. It has a useable range because of how they integrated it with the enemies and how almost everything you do gets heavily nerfed if you didn't hit the button on beat (even parrying). The bosses are also kinda a slog even if some can be easy once you learn their 3 or so attacks, usually the key to most hard stuff in this game is to parry it unfortunately. But if you don't have some high dmg parry weapon or some other combo for seriously higher dmg than normal, it can take like 4-5 minutes of just constantly shooting them while side dashing and jumping, and that gets old way faster than 4-5 minutes. Combine that with the weird but kinda necessary FOV and the i guess intentionally hard to see graphics, and its often hard to vibe to the music at all which was the main draw for me and I imagine others who weren't as informed about parrying being the real main focus of the game in addition to it having no difficulty settings. Another thing that is quite rough is while you are encouraged to parry on time like most actions, the enemies do not follow the music consistently even though they do move faster or slower based on the BPM. So often there are enemies with an audio cue that is generally jarring and plays over the music, which can cover up the beat timing of the song. The real problems though are that on top of that, they almost always spawn two of the audio cue enemies so there's more random noises over the song, with a common homing attack launching enemy playing an obnoxious gong sound very much over the song and not in time with anything. Finally, the attacks they throw out do not launch at a consistent time after the warning sound, so its more of an indication that someone in roughly whatever direction the sound came from is about to hit you.. at some point soon. Which isn't great when parrying wants you to aim at the enemy AND the bullet as well as hit the parry button on beat. You at least have a kind of shotgun range to it so its not super hard all the time to aim at the enemy and bullet, just when the chaos makes it too hard to track all of that or when the enemy attacks almost a full second later than they did the last time you heard the noise. It's really hard to play this and not constantly think "why is parry even a thing?". Maybe they felt they had to to make it challenging, because most of the time the real threats are either the things that almost guaranteed hit you hard if you don't parry it, or random cheap feeling damage from dashing backwards(which is very often necessary) into a trap, extremely long life span homing bullet, or just bumping into any enemy. The normal enemies that don't do any of those things are very often just the guys you ignore while you take out the ones who will cheap shot you or auto-hit, which over time just keeps emphasizing parrying and trying to memorize the rooms so you can still dash backwards without hitting traps at least. However, this sort of game can very much be hard without adding another mechanic that's basically separated from all the other game mechanics but also often drastically more impactful than any shooting or on beat combos can help. It just doesn't fit, i mean what even is parrying a bullet in this? We usually have guns too, do we shoot the bullet back at them? Visually it kinda just shoots a strong shot and deletes the enemy shot(or blocks it if it was melee), but even when you get like a giant laser beam of death from timing and aiming it well, it isn't particularly rewarding because it just erases a chunk of enemies and reduces the amount of shooting and moving you do, which usually are the most fun parts. The music is pretty good though! Even if it would have been even nicer if they let it shine instead of be a backdrop to 'blamblamblam GOOONG blamblam BEEP', some of the songs kick major butt and i don't think there's actually any bad music which is very cool for any game to pull off. It also has the feature of adding your own music but unfortunately its extremely limited. I was going to explain why its super limited but the review was too long so i can't. It's not a horrible game, and i did have a good amount of fun with it. It's just that those fun spots usually ended with losing patience for the parts of the game that don't seem to work well together but are pretty much all mandatory. FPS this does generally well at least, though there's not that many weapons without like finding a bunch of secrets, so it can be very limited at times there. The shooting works pretty good most of the time though, most of the clunkiness comes from the extremely slippery and wonky movement/jumping. The rest comes from the controls in general, just needing to aim and shoot while jumping and dashing constantly and having accessible buttons for parry and two side items and a slide/crouch. That's a lot of different buttons to need in a fast paced game on a keyboard where you also need to stay on WASD all the time.
